newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q2 GDP +2.2 pct, Q1 rev to +4.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q2 GDP +2.2 pct, Q1 rev to +4.9 pct.

text.p: Commerce seasonally adjusted GDP data on a chain-weighted basis. Following are annualized percent changes from prior quarters, in 1992 chain dollars. This information includes annual revisions, with previously released figures in parenthesis.
Seasonally adjusted annual rates, in blns of '92 chain dollars:
Wall Street economists had expected the advance estimate of first quarter GDP to show a 1.9 percent rise. Forecasts for the price index and the implicit price deflator were unavailable.
Commerce provides three estimates of GDP per quarter. The first is the advance (A) estimate, the second is the preliminary (P) estimate, and the last is the final (F) estimate.
The Commerce Department usually makes revisions to the national income and product accounts each July to incorporate more complete and detailed information.

In this case, it cited such factors as better information from the Internal Revenue Service on corporate tax returns as well as more current data on price changes for items like semiconductors and computers, which in many cases have fallen in real terms.
The 1.4 percent increase in the second-quarter GDP price index was the smallest increase since the third quarter of 1963, when it rose 0.7 percent, the department said.
The department also said that the 1.4 percent gain in the second-quarter implicit price deflator was the smallest increase since the second quarter of 1964, when it rose 0.9 percent.
Second quarter net exports in seasonally adjusted dollar terms fell $103.3 billion.
